audit.title: Chainlink Functions
audit.contentType: developer documentation / product overview (concept landing page)
audit.summary: This is the concept-landing page for Chainlink Functions: strong, fluent prose with a clean, self-contained opening definition that engines can lift verbatim. Its biggest weaknesses are near-total absence of concrete specifics (0 numerals: no request limits, node counts, supported-network counts, or timings) and missing machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, no canonical URL, no last-updated). A separate hard flag: the page carries a `callout="shutdown"` component yet describes the product entirely in present tense — a freshness/accuracy risk that outweighs any GEO polish, since generative engines may synthesize an active product that is being deprecated.

recommendations.title: Reconcile shutdown status with present-tense claims
recommendations.where: top of page, `<ChainlinkFunctions callout="shutdown" />` vs. body
recommendations.issue: "Chainlink Functions provides your smart contracts access to…" (present tense while a shutdown callout renders)
recommendations.change: Add a first-liftable-sentence status line stating the deprecation/shutdown state, timeline, and recommended migration path, and make the callout text machine-readable (not only a component). If still active, say so with a date.
recommendations.why: Engines lift the first self-contained sentence; a page describing a deprecated product as active produces confidently wrong answers — the highest-severity failure class.

recommendations.title: Add visible freshness + machine-readable metadata
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `dateModified`, a canonical URL, and `inLanguage`; surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: Freshness and structured metadata raise agent trust (E-E-A-T) and are the cheapest measured deficits to close.

recommendations.title: Inject concrete specifics
recommendations.issue: 0 numerals; "each node in the DON executes the code" with no counts
recommendations.change: State DON node count / threshold, max request/response byte size, execution timeout, LINK billing granularity, and the number of supported networks — with inline units.
recommendations.why: Quantitative claims are among the highest-lift changes for citation; qualitative-only prose underperforms.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifiers and add a supported-networks summary
recommendations.issue: "several community examples," "almost any Web2 system," bare link to networks page
recommendations.change: State the network count (e.g., "Supported on N mainnets and M testnets") and add a short table of chain → status inline rather than deferring entirely to another page.
recommendations.why: A self-contained answer with numbers is retrievable; a pure "see this page" pointer loses the retrieval that a summarized fact wins.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/intent-phrased headings
recommendations.issue: headings are concept-titled ("When to use"), not question-shaped
recommendations.change: Add "How does Chainlink Functions work?", "How much does Chainlink Functions cost?", and a short FAQ/troubleshooting block phrased as user questions.
recommendations.why: Devs and agents query by question/symptom; question-shaped headings win retrieval that concept prose loses.

recommendations.title: Cite primary sources for cryptographic claims
recommendations.issue: "encrypted using threshold encryption… multi-party decryption process" unattributed
recommendations.change: Link the architecture/spec page or a canonical reference for threshold encryption and DON consensus.
recommendations.why: Inline authoritative links raise credibility and citation rate.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers ("several," "most," "almost any") where numbers belong.
Present-tense product description contradicting a `shutdown` callout — a stale/accuracy signal.
Zero concrete numerals across 596 words of technical prose.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good; ensure it reflects the shutdown status.
Canonical URL and JSON-LD are template/site-level concerns; the CLI should pass raw `<head>` so metadata can be fully verified (none was captured here).
Freshness cadence and deprecation banners are site-level; ensure deprecated-product pages are dated and de-emphasized in sitemaps so engines don't over-retrieve them.
